study.title: Neural Responses of Acupuncture for Treating Functional Dyspepsia: An fMRI Study
study.randomization: computer-generated randomization sequence; randomization information was concealed from the researchers until the completion of statistical analysis
study.blinding: Patients were blinded to the group assignment; researchers blinded until completion of statistical analysis
study.population: functional dyspepsia (FD) patients recruited from the campus of Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (CDUTCM) and the Digestive Department of the Affiliated Hospital of CDUTCM
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) were aged 18 to 45 years; (2) were right-handed; (3) matched the Rome III diagnosis criteria for FD; (4) had not taken any gastrointestinal drugs or received acupuncture treatment for at least 15 days before entering the study; and (5) provided assigned informed consent
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) were pregnant or lactating; (2) had a history of head trauma with loss of consciousness or gastrointestinal surgery; (3) were currently taking drugs promoting gastrointestinal dynamics; (4) had any contraindications to acupuncture; or (5) had any MRI contraindications, such as pacemakers, fixed metal dentures, or severe claustrophobia

arms.dropouts: 1 excluded due to excessive head motion (mean framewise displacement > 0.5 mm)
4 excluded due to excessive head motion (mean framewise displacement > 0.5 mm)

conditions.timepoint_exact: baseline (after initial 2-week baseline evaluation, before treatment)
end of 4 weeks of acupuncture treatment

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: on the anterior median line of the upper abdomen, 4 cun above the navel
interventions.manipulation_exact: not_reported (see Yin et al., 2017 for protocol)
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: five acupuncture treatments per week for 4 weeks
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: two licensed acupuncturists with more than 6 years of clinical experience and who had received specialized acupuncture training in the selection of acupoints and standard acupuncture operating procedures
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: He-Mu point combination; Zhongwan (CV12) is among the most commonly used acupoints for treating gastrointestinal diseases

sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: The paper does not report any deqi, pain, or sensory sensation measures. Patients were told to maintain wakefulness during the scan. No sensation rating instruments were described.

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: blood oxygenation level-dependent fMRI (BOLD-fMRI); high-resolution three-dimensional T1-weighted imaging (3D-T1WI)
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: BOLD-fMRI: matrix size = 64 × 64; FOV = 240 × 240 mm2; slice thickness = 5 mm. 3D-T1WI: slice thickness = 1 mm; matrix size = 256 × 256; FOV = 256 × 256 mm2
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: total fMRI scans = 180, with the functional scan lasting 6 min
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: Data Processing Assistant for Resting-State fMRI (DPARSF) software in MATLAB (MathWorks, Inc., Natick, MA, United States)
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: Data Processing Assistant for Resting-State fMRI (DPARSF) software in MATLAB
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 6-mm3 full width at half maximum (FWHM)
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Patients with excessive head motion [with mean frame-wise displacement greater than 0.5 mm (Power et al., 2012)] were excluded from the analysis
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: band-pass filtered with a frequency window of 0.01–0.08 Hz
statistical_thresholds_exact: ALFF analysis: voxel-level p < 0.005 and corrected cluster-level p < 0.05 (GRF correction)

extraction_notes.note: No deqi, pain, or any other sensory/interoceptive sensation measures were reported in this study. The paper does not mention any sensation rating instruments being administered to participants.

No expectancy, credibility, blinding success, or allocation guessing measures were reported. The paper states patients were blinded to group assignment but provides no formal blinding check instrument or outcome.
No adverse events were reported or mentioned in the paper. It is unclear whether adverse events were systematically assessed.

The paper states the acupuncture treatment protocol used is outlined in a previous study (Yin et al., 2017) and refers the reader there. Detailed needle manipulation, depth, deqi intention, and retention time for individual acupoints are not provided in this paper.

The BOLD-fMRI acquisition parameters include slice number = 30 and flip angle = 90°. Slice thickness is 5 mm but no gap is reported. Voxel dimensions in mm are not directly stated (only matrix size and FOV).

Table 3 lists Middle frontal gyrus for Group B with L/R labeled as 'R' but the x-coordinate is −30, which is typically left hemisphere. This discrepancy was preserved as-is from the table and noted in the coordinate_space_inference_note for nc_004_r3.

The total number randomized is inferred as 38 (stated: '38 eligible patients were randomly assigned'), and 5 were excluded for motion, leaving 33. The exact split of dropouts per arm (1 from group A vs 4 from group B to reach 18 and 15 respectively from 19 each) is inferred from n_assigned = 19 per group. The paper does not explicitly state n_assigned per group; 19+19=38 total randomized is the inference.

The cluster extent units in Table 3 are not explicitly labeled. 'Cluster sizes' of 280, 274, 245, 338, 791, 854, 307 are assumed to be in voxels based on standard DPARSF/SPM reporting conventions, but the paper does not explicitly state the unit.

No ALFF coordinate table is provided for the left postcentral gyrus result (nc_001). Peak MNI coordinates and cluster size/T-value for the ALFF finding are not reported in the text or any table. The result is described narratively and shown in Figure 2A.
No between-group comparison of rsFC changes (group A vs group B) was reported; only within-group changes are provided.
Needle retention time per session is not reported in this paper; readers are referred to Yin et al., 2017.

The paper reports no correlation between FC and clinical efficacy in group A and group B separately, only the overall (combined) ALFF–SID correlation. This is stated explicitly: 'there was no significant correlation between FC and clinical efficacy in group A and group B.'
BOLD-fMRI additional parameters: 3D-T1WI slices = 176. The number of functional BOLD slices is 30. Global signal regression is not mentioned. White matter/CSF nuisance regression is not mentioned.
Peak-only re-extraction: 0 contrasts updated, 2 new contrasts added
